paragraphs: There were two girls, daughters of the same mother. As they came home from the fair, they saw a very handsome young man standing at the door of the house ahead of them. They had never seen such a handsome man before. He had gold on his cap, gold on his finger, gold around his neck, and a red-gold watch chain—oh, he had money! He held a golden ball in each hand. He gave each girl a ball, which she had to keep. If she lost it, she was to be hanged. One of the girls—the younger one—lost her ball. I’ll tell you how. She was beside the wooden fence around a park, tossing her ball. It went up, and up, and up, until it went right over the fence. When she climbed up to look, the ball rolled along the green grass, straight to the door of the house. It went inside, and she saw it no more.
So she was taken away to be hanged by the neck until she was dead, because she had lost her ball.

But she had a sweetheart, and he said he would go and get the ball. He went to the park gate, but it was shut, so he climbed the hedge. When he reached the top, an old woman rose from the ditch in front of him. She said that if he wanted to get the ball, he must sleep three nights in the house. He said he would.
Then he went into the house and looked for the ball, but could not find it. Night came, and he heard goblins moving in the courtyard. He looked out of the window, and the yard was full of them.

Soon he heard footsteps coming upstairs. He hid behind the door, as quiet as a mouse. In came a great giant, five times as tall as he was. The giant looked around but did not see the young man, so he went to the window and bent down to look out. As he leaned on his elbows to watch the goblins in the yard, the young man stepped behind him and cut him in half with one blow of his sword. The top half fell into the yard, and the bottom half stood looking out of the window.
The goblins gave a great cry when they saw half the giant tumbling down towards them. They called out, “Here comes half our master! Give us the other half.”

So the young man said, “There’s no point in you, a pair of legs, standing alone at the window when you have no eyes to see with. Go and join your brother.” He threw the giant’s lower half after the upper half. Once the goblins had the whole giant, they fell quiet.

The next night, the young man was at the house again. This time a second giant came through the door, and as he entered, the young man cut him in half. But the legs walked on to the chimney and went up it. “Go on, follow your legs,” the young man said to the head, and threw that up the chimney too.
On the third night, the young man got into bed. He heard the goblins struggling underneath it. They had the ball there and were throwing it back and forth.

Now one of them sticks a leg out from under the bed, so the young man brings down his sword and cuts it off. Then another sticks an arm out on the other side, and he cuts that off. At last he had maimed them all. They all went off crying and wailing, and forgot the ball. He took it from under the bed and went to find his true love.
Now the girl had been taken to York to be hanged. She was brought onto the scaffold, and the hangman said, “Now, girl, you must hang by the neck until you are dead.” But she cried out:

“Stop, stop, I think I see my mother coming!
Oh, Mother, have you brought my golden ball
And come to set me free?”
“I have not brought your golden ball
Or come to set you free,
But I have come to see you hanged
Upon these gallows.”
Then the hangman said, “Now, girl, say your prayers, for you must die.” But she said:

“Stop, stop, I think I see my father coming!
Oh, Father, have you brought my golden ball
And come to set me free?”
“I have not brought your golden ball
Or come to set you free,
But I have come to see you hanged
Upon these gallows.”
Then the hangman said, “Have you finished your prayers? Now, girl, put your head into the noose.”

But she answered, “Stop, stop, I think I see my brother coming!” And she sang again. Then she thought she saw her sister coming, then her uncle, then her aunt, then her cousin. But after this the hangman said, “I will wait no longer. You’re making a fool of me. You must be hanged at once.”
But now she saw her sweetheart coming through the crowd, holding her own golden ball high above his head. So she said:

“Stop, stop, I see my sweetheart coming!
Sweetheart, have you brought my golden ball
And come to set me free?”
“Yes, I have brought your golden ball
And come to set you free.
I have not come to see you hanged
Upon these gallows.”
And he took her home, and they lived happily ever after.
